title: Follow-up decisions: nodules, angina, counts and labs

source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-10-09, from the ABFM 2025 In-Training Examination critiques, items 9, 10, 11, 14 and 22. Each question cites its item. Provisional grouping; review before trusting.

questions.q: An incidental 6-mm solid lung nodule in a 50-year-old who has never smoked. What is next?
questions.why: The interval flexes to 3 to 6 months for worrying features or patient preference. Biopsy is not for a small solid nodule in a non-smoker.

questions.q: A solid lung nodule is called benign once unchanged for how long?
questions.why: Subsolid nodules are followed longer, since they grow slowly and carry a higher risk of being malignant.

questions.q: Which incidental lung nodule warrants referral to a pulmonologist?
d: A 6-mm solid nodule in a non-smoker
A solid nodule unchanged for 3 years
questions.why: Along with solid nodules of 8 to 30 mm. Subsolid nodules carry a higher probability of malignancy at any size.

questions.q: Chest pain, normal troponins, intermediate risk, a negative stress test six months ago. What is the next test?
questions.why: A stress test negative within the year is not repeated. The angiogram shows whether there is obstructive disease or plaque; MRI answers structural questions.

questions.q: Where does CT fractional flow reserve fit in the evaluation of chest pain?
questions.a: After CT angiography shows a stenosis, to guide revascularisation
d: As the first test in a low-risk patient
Instead of troponin in the emergency department
questions.why: It estimates whether a stenosis seen on the angiogram limits flow, which is the question that decides on intervention.

questions.q: Angina on carvedilol with a heart rate of 52, normal ejection fraction, stage 4 CKD. What is added?
questions.why: A second first-line class once the first is at its tolerated maximum. The bradycardia blocks the beta blocker increase; clopidogrel does nothing for symptoms. Watch the blood pressure after the nitrate.

questions.q: What is the guidance on ivabradine for angina in chronic coronary disease with a normal ejection fraction?
d: Added when the heart rate stays over 70
Reserved for failure of three other classes
questions.why: Ranolazine is the drug kept for patients already on two other classes, and cost is its main drawback.

questions.q: Stable on antiretroviral therapy for ten years. Which tests are routine for everyone?
a: A glomerular filtration rate at least twice yearly
questions.why: The kidney tests catch drug nephrotoxicity. Bone density is for those at risk, neurocognitive testing is by indication, and Framingham is not validated in HIV.

questions.q: In whom on antiretroviral therapy is liver fibrosis screening appropriate?
questions.why: The hepatitis viruses, not the antiretrovirals, drive fibrosis. A raised ALT prompts a work-up, not a screening programme.

questions.q: Known immune thrombocytopenia, no bleeding, platelets 47,000. What treatment is given?
questions.why: Steroids, intravenous immunoglobulin and rituximab are all used when treatment is needed. Hydroxychloroquine is not.

questions.q: Below what platelet count is immune thrombocytopenia treated even without bleeding?
questions.why: Active bleeding is the other trigger, at any count. The family physician decides whether to act today; the haematologist owns the long game.
